capabilities: read EPUB, PDF, MOBI, FB2, AZW3, CBZ and text files with progress tracking and bookmarks
aggregate highlights and comments into a per-book Markdown note with links back to the source passage
chat with configured AI services about selections, pages or full text PDFs and save replies as notes
translate or look up selections, save vocabulary entries, and review them via Spaced Repetition or sync to Anki
send ebooks to a jailbroken Kindle over Wi-Fi and browse or download books from Gutenberg and Hacker Books
extras: Optional 'Qiaomu Library' book downloads require an activation code with per-device and daily quotas; reading itself is local and offline. The README includes a detailed privacy table of what each optional feature sends and notes limits such as no OCR for scanned PDFs. Six public-domain starter books ship with the plugin.
motivation: The author built it to keep reading, in-place questioning, note saving and returning to the source in one workflow, reducing back-and-forth between reader, chat and note apps.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in book reader, so reading, asking questions about a text, and saving highlights means copying between a reader app, a chat window and notes.

requires.name: Spaced Repetition (vocabulary review) and AnkiConnect (Anki sync)
Calibre (book import) and a jailbroken Kindle with KOReader (book transfer)
AI model services and cloud TTS providers
CLI logins such as Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, Grok CLI, Kimi Code CLI, ZCode CLI

summary: Ebook reader for EPUB, PDF, MOBI, FB2, AZW3, CBZ and text formats that ties highlights, per-book Markdown notes, optional AI chat, translation, vocabulary review and read-aloud into one reading workflow.
